messages:
emma: Proposal: use an epoch-based bootstrap handshake for air-gapped installs. Agent pulls a single signed epoch manifest, verifies chain-of-trust, then fetches content blobs referenced by manifest. Reason: reduces repeated signature work and lets us revoke windows.

raj: Can you sketch the handshake? curious about atomic activation and rollback.

emma: Flow:
1) seed image contains agent + pubkey
2) on admin trigger agent fetches epoch-manifest (signed)
3) manifest lists bundle roots + epoch id + activation window
4) agent downloads objects (content-addressed), verifies hashes and sig chain
5) installs into staging dir
6) at activation time do atomic rename + state ledger append

oliver: How do we keep manifest delivery working for air-gapped customers? they may not allow outbound.

sasha: Ops usually push via USB or local registry. Manifest can be delivered as a single artifact (tar.gz) that includes the blobstore and a lightweight sqlite ledger. Agent can verify locally. We should support both pull and push.

emma: Key tradeoffs: signed epoch reduces per-object sigs but requires trust in epoch signing key rotation. Need CRL/epoch revocation mechanism. Also activation window needs monotonicity to avoid replay.

raj: About rollback: what if new epoch installs but activation fails? we keep last-activated symlink and use retained staging dirs. Also ledger entry includes previous epoch hash for fast rollback.

deploy-bot: New RFC draft uploaded: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/epoch-bootstrap (internal) :white_check_mark:

oliver: For incremental updates, we can send small delta layers as content-addressed blobs and rely on agent dedupe. But we must watch memory when streaming large models.

sasha: Operational note: add `--verify-only` mode so support can precheck manifests before activation.

emma: I'll add a small proto:
```json
{
  "epoch_id": "2026-03-15T00:00Z",
  "signed_by": "redwood-release@keys:v2",
  "activation_window": "2026-04-01T00:00Z/2026-04-07T00:00Z",
  "roots": ["sha256:abcd..."],
  "objects": [
    {"path":"model.bin","sha256":"...","size":"123456789"},
    {"path":"runtime.tar.gz","sha256":"...","size":"12345"}
  ]
}
```

raj: LGTM. Emma, can you add a failure-mode matrix? I'd like to see network partials, disk full, signature mismatch.

emma: Will do, thanks :v:
